chapter: Band in New York and London
title: A cooperative band of friends, and the two-beat style
summary: The band split money five ways with LaRocca as business manager; records played; March syncopated style.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: Well, before we play this record, let me just ask you one thing, Nick. There's been a lot of misunderstanding. The original Dixieland jazz band was composed of good friends. Isn't this so?
We were all good friends. That's right.

We had no enemies. It was a cooperative band, and the money was split equally. I did all the business for the band. I did the leading on getting the jobs, and everything else was my job. And when it came to splitting the money up, it was a five-way split. There's some of the boys still living. They'll tell you they got what's coming to them.

Yes, well, that's what a lot of people don't realize, that these men are still around. It's not quite as long ago as we'd like to think. So many people think that the original Dixieland jazz band was something that was around just before the Revolutionary War.
Well, that was caused by a lot of modern-day writers.

Yes, I know. And that's why we're so anxious to get all of your messages we can, Nick LaRocca. But at this time, let's let our audience hear the tune that you fellas composed while you were in England called The Satanic Blues. This is my mistake, Nick. We had set up Delivery Stable Blues, and we just talked our way right through it. They have never heard it, so we are now playing Delivery Stable Blues. We'll come back to Satanic Blues in a moment. The Satanic Blues The Satanic Blues The Satanic Blues The Satanic Blues The Satanic Blues And that was the Delivery Stable Blues. We've got so many interesting things that we wanted to talk to Mr. LaRocca about, but we had promised to you that we would play the Satanic Blues, but we won't be able to play too much because we have an extremely interesting story coming up. So now that we're ready, let's hear at least a portion of The Satanic Blues. The Satanic Blues We're very sorry that we couldn't finish the whole thing, but we believe that our message is just as important as the music. Now, back to Nick LaRocca. Nick, that is in the real tradition of two-beat music, as we call it, which was the original Dixieland beat. Is that correct? That's correct. And that's the only type of music you fellas knew how to play.
And this was the music that you say had been born in Chicago as a sudden inspiration from the bandstand, that you had watched people dance.
That's right. But all New Orleans bars.
